name: Temples of Kanchipuram
theme: Kanchipuram's great Shiva and Vishnu shrines — the Earth Lingam, the Pallava sandstone masterpiece, the presiding Goddess, and the city's Divya Desams
description: Kanchipuram, the ancient Pallava capital and one of the seven sacred cities of Hinduism, has long been called the city of a thousand temples, and its devotion still divides between two quarters. In Shiva Kanchi stand Ekambareswarar, the city's largest temple, where Shiva is worshipped as the Prithvi Lingam of the Earth beneath a soaring Vijayanagara gateway; Kailasanathar, carved from soft sandstone by the Pallava king Rajasimha at the dawn of the eighth century, the prototype from which South Indian temple architecture grew; Kachabeswarar, a Shiva shrine sung in the Thevaram hymns; and Kamakshi, presiding goddess of Kanchi and one of the foremost Shakti shrines of the South. In Vishnu Kanchi, the city's Divya Desams gather around Varadaraja on his little hill of Hastagiri, the towering Ulagalantha with the shrines that share its courtyard, and the three-storeyed Pallava Vaikunta Perumal, with smaller sanctums sung by the Alvars tucked among the lanes. Walked slowly, the two quarters read as a single pilgrimage.
